SELECT time, text FROM (
  SELECT r.ts/1000.0 AS time, r.value AS value,
         LAG(r.value) OVER (ORDER BY r.ts) AS previous,
         'DC current started' AS text
  FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
  WHERE s.key = 'dc_charging' AND r.ts < 2000000000000
)
WHERE value <> 0 AND (previous IS NULL OR previous = 0)
  AND time BETWEEN $__from/1000.0 AND $__to/1000.0
ORDER BY time

description: The charge manager (CAN 0x605/0x610/0x615/0x620/0x625): the DC current the vehicle requests, the three limits that bound it, the state machine, and the fault source and code. The only signals on this bus that see a DC fast charge — the onboard charger's frames are silent through one.

options.content:
The charge manager, CAN `0x605` / `0x610` / `0x615` / `0x620` / `0x625`, decoded in
`src/can/charge-manager.ts`. The evidence for every byte — factory DBC names, match rates over 29
charge sessions, and the hypotheses that were refuted — is in `docs/charge-manager.md`. This tab
exists because **these are the only signals on this bus that see a DC fast charge at all**: the
onboard charger's frames (`0x305`/`0x306`, the *Charging* tab) go completely silent during one, so
`mains_a`, `dc_a` and `dc_v` all read "nothing happening" while 20 kW goes into the pack. Measured,
not assumed: across the 18-minute DC session of 2026-08-04 19:58-20:16 those four keys logged **zero
rows between them**, while `fast_dc_target_a` logged 93 and peaked at 66 A against a measured `pack_a`
of 66.3 A.

**Three names that look alike and are not.** Read the qualifier, not the prefix:

| what | key | frame |
| --- | --- | --- |
| what the RIDER picked on the bike's screen | `dc_charge_limit_selected_a` | `0x121` b2 |
| the bike's own configured ceiling, `MAX_DC_CHG_CURRENT` (VCU parameter 258, a static 75 A) | `fast_dc_limit_max_a` | `0x625` b2 |
| what the STATION offers, i.e. the limit in force this second | `fast_dc_limit_a` | `0x620` b0 |

`0x625` b2 is **the vehicle's own configuration** and has nothing to do with the station — it reads
75 in 100.000 % of 1 571 614 frames, parked and unplugged included. `0x620` b0 points the other way:
`CM_EVSE_FDB` is **CM → VCU**, so b0 is **what the station offers**, relayed inward by the charge
manager — which is why it reacts to a derate rather than commanding one. `0x615` b2 is the current
the vehicle **asks for**, not one it measures: it leads the first amp of every captured ramp by
0.03-2.40 s, which a readback cannot do. The delivered current on these
panels is `pack_a` off `0x200`, which is a measurement.

**Why a flat line can mean "the sender left".** Four of the five frames are on the bus only while a
charge cable is live, and the log stores a row only when a value changes. So when the cable comes
out, **eleven of the fifteen keys simply stop** — every one except `0x625`'s four — and every
step-held panel carries their last value onwards for as long as you ask it to. In the 2026-08-04
capture `charge_type`'s last row is 18 minutes before the session ends and it still reads DC ten
minutes after that. A tile reading "DC" days after a charge is this, not a live session.

**`0x625` is the exception and is what closes the picture.** It broadcasts at 10 Hz whenever the
bike is awake, so `dc_charging` and `ac_charging` really do write a 0 when the current stops — read
them *with* the charge-path tile, not instead of it. Both are worded "current is FLOWING", not "a
session exists": through the 155 s aborted DC attempt of 2026-08-09 14:42 they stay 0 while
`0x605` and `0x610` both report an established DC session.

**Row cost.** All fifteen keys together wrote **176 rows** across that entire 18-minute DC session,
93 of them `fast_dc_target_a`, against 267 890 rows from every signal in the same 47-minute capture.
Nothing here carries a deadband and nothing needs one.

**2060 rows.** Every query on this tab carries `AND r.ts < 2000000000000`. The Pi has no RTC and
logs with a bad clock until `gps/clock.ts` steps it from satellite time, which put 49 772 real
readings — including 1 740 of `pack_a` and 33 of `odometer_can_km` — in the year 2060. Without the
guard, any absolute range ending past 2033 stretches every axis here to 2060 and turns a charge
session into a sliver, and the held-value tiles would report a 2060 row as "now". ⚠️ **No other
dashboard in this folder carries that guard**; they are safe only for as long as their default
`to: now` range is left alone.

panels.description: `charge_type`, 0x605 b2: 1 = AC, 2 = DC. A property of the SESSION, not of current flowing — it reads 2 for the whole 155 s of the aborted DC attempt of 2026-08-09 14:42 while not one amp moves. Held rather than range-bounded: the frame behind it is on the bus only while a cable is live, so a window with no session contains no row and a bounded tile would read "No data" — indistinguishable from the logger being down (grafana/README.md). ⚠️ 0x605 stops when the cable comes out, so this tile holds the last path indefinitely; read it next to the two flowing tiles, which come off 0x625 and do close themselves.

targets.rawQueryText:
SELECT r.ts/1000.0 AS time, r.value AS "Charge path"
FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
WHERE s.key = 'charge_type' AND r.ts <= $__to AND r.ts < 2000000000000
ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1

Held rather than range-bounded: the frame behind it is on the bus only while a cable is live, so a window with no session contains no row and a bounded tile would read "No data" — indistinguishable from the logger being down (grafana/README.md).

HAVING COUNT(*) > 0

panels.description: The four session-level flags, each seeded from the last row before the range so a session that started off-screen still draws (grafana/README.md). ⚠️ The two flowing lanes come off 0x625, which broadcasts whenever the bike is awake, so they close themselves. The charge-path and isolation lanes come off 0x605, which stops with the cable — their last region runs to the right edge whether the cable is still in or not. `bms_leak_detect_inhibit` is the VCU COMMANDING the insulation monitor off (V_IMD_DISABLE); the monitor cannot run against a station-driven DC bus, so it is inhibited for exactly the duration of a DC session, 99.933 % of 156 931 frames.

targets.rawQueryText:
SELECT time, "DC current (0x625 b4 bit 5)" FROM (
  SELECT r.ts/1000.0 AS time, CASE WHEN r.value <> 0 THEN 'flowing' ELSE 'no' END AS "DC current (0x625 b4 bit 5)"
  FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
  WHERE s.key = 'dc_charging' AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to AND r.ts < 2000000000000
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM (SELECT $__from/1000.0, CASE WHEN r.value <> 0 THEN 'flowing' ELSE 'no' END
                 FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
                 WHERE s.key = 'dc_charging' AND r.ts < $__from AND r.ts < 2000000000000
                 ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1)
)
ORDER BY time

  SELECT r.ts/1000.0 AS time, CASE WHEN r.value <> 0 THEN 'flowing' ELSE 'no' END AS "AC current (0x625 b4 bit 2)"
  FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
  WHERE s.key = 'ac_charging' AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to AND r.ts < 2000000000000
  UNION ALL

                 FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
                 WHERE s.key = 'ac_charging' AND r.ts < $__from AND r.ts < 2000000000000

)
ORDER BY time

SELECT time, "Charge path (0x605 b2)" FROM (
  SELECT r.ts/1000.0 AS time, CASE CAST(r.value AS INTEGER) WHEN 1 THEN 'AC' WHEN 2 THEN 'DC' ELSE 'none' END AS "Charge path (0x605 b2)"
  FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id

SELECT time, "Isolation monitor (0x605 b7)" FROM (
  SELECT r.ts/1000.0 AS time, CASE WHEN r.value <> 0 THEN 'inhibited' ELSE 'running' END AS "Isolation monitor (0x605 b7)"
  FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id

                 ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1)
)

panels.title: Session lanes
DC current — what was asked for, what bounded it, what arrived

panels.description:
The whole DC current story on one axis, because all five really are the same quantity. **requested** is what the vehicle asks the station for and leads the first amp by 0.03-2.40 s. **delivered** is `pack_a` off the BMS, positive while charging — against the request r = +0.9951 with the pack drawing a median 0.30 A less. **limit in force** is what the STATION offers, relayed inward on `CM_EVSE_FDB` (CM → VCU) — which is why it reacts rather than commands: on 2026-08-04 it fell 75 → 64 eleven seconds AFTER the delivered current had already dropped to 55.6 A. ⚠️ "In force" is not "binding": it equals the request in only 0.005 % of 151 202 aligned samples, so the corpus holds essentially no observation of this ceiling ever constraining the delivery. **bike ceiling** is this vehicle's own configured 75 A and is not an offer from the station. **rider's selection** is the dial on the bike's screen and only writes a row when the dial MOVES — re-picking the value you already had writes nothing.

⚠️ `pack_a` is the pack's current in both directions, so a ride inside the range squashes the charge: across the 199 368 non-2060 `pack_a` rows in `rides.db` the 1st percentile is −172.3 A and the minimum −405.2 A, against a charge that never reaches +75. Zoom to the session; the annotations mark where they start. ⚠️ And both series are logged on change, so they step at different instants: pairing the 2026-08-04 session's 23 post-ramp request samples with the last `pack_a` before each gives a mean gap of +0.5 A but individual pairs from −5.4 to +6.2 A. Read a several-amp difference at a step as alignment, not as the station missing the request.

Seeded at both ends so the ceiling and the rider's dial — which log roughly once per boot — still draw in a window that contains no boot. A flat line therefore means "unchanged", except at the far right, where for the four cable-only signals it can also mean the sender left with the cable.

targets.rawQueryText:
-- Amps from five different places. See the panel description for which is which;
-- 0x625 b2 is the BIKE's configured ceiling and not anything the station offered.
SELECT time, metric, value FROM (
  SELECT r.ts/1000.0 AS time,
         CASE s.key
                WHEN 'fast_dc_target_a' THEN 'requested (0x615 b2)'
                WHEN 'pack_a' THEN 'delivered — pack current (0x200)'
                WHEN 'fast_dc_limit_a' THEN 'limit in force (0x620 b0)'
                WHEN 'fast_dc_limit_max_a' THEN 'bike ceiling, MAX_DC_CHG_CURRENT (0x625 b2)'
                WHEN 'dc_charge_limit_selected_a' THEN 'rider selection (0x121)'
         END AS metric,
         r.value AS value
  FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
  WHERE s.key IN ('fast_dc_target_a', 'pack_a', 'fast_dc_limit_a', 'fast_dc_limit_max_a', 'dc_charge_limit_selected_a') AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to AND r.ts < 2000000000000
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM (SELECT r.ts/1000.0, 'requested (0x615 b2)', r.value
                 FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
                 WHERE s.key = 'fast_dc_target_a' AND r.ts < $__from AND r.ts < 2000000000000
                 ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM (SELECT r.ts/1000.0, 'delivered — pack current (0x200)', r.value
                 FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
                 WHERE s.key = 'pack_a' AND r.ts < $__from AND r.ts < 2000000000000
                 ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM (SELECT r.ts/1000.0, 'limit in force (0x620 b0)', r.value
                 FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
                 WHERE s.key = 'fast_dc_limit_a' AND r.ts < $__from AND r.ts < 2000000000000
                 ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM (SELECT r.ts/1000.0, 'bike ceiling, MAX_DC_CHG_CURRENT (0x625 b2)', r.value
                 FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
                 WHERE s.key = 'fast_dc_limit_max_a' AND r.ts < $__from AND r.ts < 2000000000000
                 ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM (SELECT r.ts/1000.0, 'rider selection (0x121)', r.value
                 FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
                 WHERE s.key = 'dc_charge_limit_selected_a' AND r.ts < $__from AND r.ts < 2000000000000
                 ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM (SELECT $__to/1000.0, 'requested (0x615 b2)', r.value
                 FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
                 WHERE s.key = 'fast_dc_target_a' AND r.ts <= $__to AND r.ts < 2000000000000
                 ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM (SELECT $__to/1000.0, 'delivered — pack current (0x200)', r.value
                 FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
                 WHERE s.key = 'pack_a' AND r.ts <= $__to AND r.ts < 2000000000000
                 ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM (SELECT $__to/1000.0, 'limit in force (0x620 b0)', r.value
                 FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
                 WHERE s.key = 'fast_dc_limit_a' AND r.ts <= $__to AND r.ts < 2000000000000
                 ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM (SELECT $__to/1000.0, 'bike ceiling, MAX_DC_CHG_CURRENT (0x625 b2)', r.value
                 FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
                 WHERE s.key = 'fast_dc_limit_max_a' AND r.ts <= $__to AND r.ts < 2000000000000
                 ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM (SELECT $__to/1000.0, 'rider selection (0x121)', r.value
                 FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
                 WHERE s.key = 'dc_charge_limit_selected_a' AND r.ts <= $__to AND r.ts < 2000000000000
                 ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1)
)
ORDER BY time

panels.title: DC current: requested, in force, delivered
DC voltage and the SOC the station is told

panels.description: `fast_dc_target_v` (0x615 b0-1, 16-bit LE) is the voltage the vehicle REQUESTS, and it tracks the pack at slope 1.0 with a median gap of +13.40 V (p5 12.70, p95 14.60) in every mode including AC and idle. `fast_dc_limit_max_v` (0x625 b0-1) is the configured ceiling — a static 363 V that moved once, to 371 V, 91 s into a DC session on 2026-08-09 and never moved back. ⚠️ `fast_dc_target_v` REPLACED `charge_manager_pack_v` on 2026-08-20 and is 13.5 V higher for the same bytes; rows logged under the old key are a different quantity and are deliberately not unioned in here.

targets.rawQueryText:
-- The request, the measurement it sits above, and the configured ceiling.
SELECT time, metric, value FROM (
  SELECT r.ts/1000.0 AS time,
         CASE s.key
                WHEN 'fast_dc_target_v' THEN 'target (0x615 b0-1)'
                WHEN 'pack_v' THEN 'pack (0x200)'
                WHEN 'fast_dc_limit_max_v' THEN 'configured V limit (0x625 b0-1)'
         END AS metric,
         r.value AS value
  FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
  WHERE s.key IN ('fast_dc_target_v', 'pack_v', 'fast_dc_limit_max_v') AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to AND r.ts < 2000000000000
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM (SELECT r.ts/1000.0, 'target (0x615 b0-1)', r.value
                 FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
                 WHERE s.key = 'fast_dc_target_v' AND r.ts < $__from AND r.ts < 2000000000000
                 ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM (SELECT r.ts/1000.0, 'pack (0x200)', r.value
                 FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
                 WHERE s.key = 'pack_v' AND r.ts < $__from AND r.ts < 2000000000000
                 ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM (SELECT r.ts/1000.0, 'configured V limit (0x625 b0-1)', r.value
                 FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
                 WHERE s.key = 'fast_dc_limit_max_v' AND r.ts < $__from AND r.ts < 2000000000000
                 ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM (SELECT $__to/1000.0, 'target (0x615 b0-1)', r.value
                 FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
                 WHERE s.key = 'fast_dc_target_v' AND r.ts <= $__to AND r.ts < 2000000000000
                 ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM (SELECT $__to/1000.0, 'pack (0x200)', r.value
                 FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
                 WHERE s.key = 'pack_v' AND r.ts <= $__to AND r.ts < 2000000000000
                 ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM (SELECT $__to/1000.0, 'configured V limit (0x625 b0-1)', r.value
                 FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
                 WHERE s.key = 'fast_dc_limit_max_v' AND r.ts <= $__to AND r.ts < 2000000000000
                 ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1)
)
ORDER BY time

panels.title: DC voltage: target vs pack

panels.description: `charge_manager_soc` (0x615 b3) is the SOC the VCU reports OUTWARD for the station's ramp planning, and it is free to disagree with the BMS — it equals `soc` in 99.008 % of the 847 644 frames from 2026-08-02 20:48 onwards, and before that ran 2-4 % low for every frame of five sessions. Kept under its own key for exactly that reason; where the two lines separate is the interesting part.

targets.rawQueryText:
-- Two SOCs that are allowed to disagree.
SELECT time, metric, value FROM (
  SELECT r.ts/1000.0 AS time,
         CASE s.key
                WHEN 'charge_manager_soc' THEN 'reported to station (0x615 b3)'
                WHEN 'soc' THEN 'BMS SOC (0x200)'
         END AS metric,
         r.value AS value
  FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
  WHERE s.key IN ('charge_manager_soc', 'soc') AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to AND r.ts < 2000000000000
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM (SELECT r.ts/1000.0, 'reported to station (0x615 b3)', r.value
                 FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
                 WHERE s.key = 'charge_manager_soc' AND r.ts < $__from AND r.ts < 2000000000000
                 ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM (SELECT r.ts/1000.0, 'BMS SOC (0x200)', r.value
                 FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
                 WHERE s.key = 'soc' AND r.ts < $__from AND r.ts < 2000000000000
                 ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM (SELECT $__to/1000.0, 'reported to station (0x615 b3)', r.value
                 FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
                 WHERE s.key = 'charge_manager_soc' AND r.ts <= $__to AND r.ts < 2000000000000
                 ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM (SELECT $__to/1000.0, 'BMS SOC (0x200)', r.value
                 FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
                 WHERE s.key = 'soc' AND r.ts <= $__to AND r.ts < 2000000000000
                 ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1)
)
ORDER BY time

panels.title: SOC: reported to the station vs the BMS's own

panels.description: One raw byte, five factory fields. The DC setup of 2026-08-04 walks 0x10 → 0x08 → 0x0A → 0x2A → 0x4A → 0x5A → 0x5E over **26.1 s** (19:58:19.252 → 19:58:45.346 — ten seconds only gets as far as 0x5A), which reads on these lanes as inlet detected → mode DC → authorisation → inlet locked → relay closed. ⚠️ Teardown is NOT that in reverse: 0x5E → 0x5A → 0x4A → 0x48 in 1.5 s at 20:16:03-04, mirroring two steps and then ending on 0x48, a value that never appeared during setup — and the lanes are what make that legible, since 0x48 is inlet still present with WAIT_AUTH still at 2, mode and lock already dropped. 0x5E is the settled DC value and 0x19 the settled AC one. ⚠️ Ours was read as "bit 0 = AC, bit 1 = DC" until 2026-08-20; the corpus says otherwise — the pair is never 3 in 968 629 frames, which is what an enum looks like and not what two flags look like.

targets.rawQueryText:
-- 0x610 b0 is logged whole, because a raw byte survives a bit-position error and split
-- fields do not. The split back out happens here instead. Layout and match rates:
-- docs/charge-manager.md §0x610. Each of the three 2-bit fields is an ENUM and none of
-- them ever reaches 3 in 968 629 frames, which is how they were told apart from flags.
SELECT time, "Mode request (CM_CHGMODE_REQ)", "Relay request (CM_RELAY_REQ)", "Inlet present (CM_INL_STS)", "Inlet locked (CM_INL_LKSTS)", "Authorisation (WAIT_AUTH)" FROM (
  SELECT r.ts/1000.0 AS time,
         CASE CAST(r.value AS INTEGER) & 3 WHEN 0 THEN 'none' WHEN 1 THEN 'AC' WHEN 2 THEN 'DC' ELSE 'reserved 3' END AS "Mode request (CM_CHGMODE_REQ)",
         CASE WHEN (CAST(r.value AS INTEGER) >> 2) & 1 THEN 'requested' ELSE 'no' END AS "Relay request (CM_RELAY_REQ)",
         CASE WHEN (CAST(r.value AS INTEGER) >> 3) & 1 THEN 'present' ELSE 'no' END AS "Inlet present (CM_INL_STS)",
         CASE WHEN (CAST(r.value AS INTEGER) >> 4) & 1 THEN 'locked' ELSE 'no' END AS "Inlet locked (CM_INL_LKSTS)",
         CASE (CAST(r.value AS INTEGER) >> 5) & 3 WHEN 0 THEN 'none' WHEN 1 THEN 'auth 1' WHEN 2 THEN 'auth 2' ELSE 'reserved 3' END AS "Authorisation (WAIT_AUTH)"
  FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
  WHERE s.key = 'charge_manager_status' AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to AND r.ts < 2000000000000
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM (SELECT $__from/1000.0,
                        CASE CAST(r.value AS INTEGER) & 3 WHEN 0 THEN 'none' WHEN 1 THEN 'AC' WHEN 2 THEN 'DC' ELSE 'reserved 3' END,
                        CASE WHEN (CAST(r.value AS INTEGER) >> 2) & 1 THEN 'requested' ELSE 'no' END,
                        CASE WHEN (CAST(r.value AS INTEGER) >> 3) & 1 THEN 'present' ELSE 'no' END,
                        CASE WHEN (CAST(r.value AS INTEGER) >> 4) & 1 THEN 'locked' ELSE 'no' END,
                        CASE (CAST(r.value AS INTEGER) >> 5) & 3 WHEN 0 THEN 'none' WHEN 1 THEN 'auth 1' WHEN 2 THEN 'auth 2' ELSE 'reserved 3' END
                 FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
                 WHERE s.key = 'charge_manager_status' AND r.ts < $__from AND r.ts < 2000000000000
                 ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1)
)
ORDER BY time

panels.title: Charge-manager status (0x610 b0), split into its factory fields

panels.description: The cleanest AC/DC discriminator on this bus: 0x23 while DC current flows (99.974 % of 151 096 frames) and 0x02 while AC mains flows (99.999 % of 784 599). Only those two are named; everything between renders as raw hex, and the log is why: **the handshake is not one fixed sequence**. Out of 0x02, 2026-08-04 19:58 goes 0x14 → 0x04 → 0x07 → 0x0D → 0x11 → 0x12 → 0x11 → 0x23 over 4.70 s, with 0x11 on both sides of 0x12; the aborted attempt of 2026-08-09 14:41 goes 0x14 → 0x04 → 0x07 → 0x09 → 0x23 in 3.70 s, through an 0x09 neither other session shows; its retry 66 s later goes 0x14 → 0x04 → 0x23 in 2.10 s. Three sessions, three paths, so no state table is inferred here — and the factory DBC does not name this byte at all. ⚠️ These are 10 Hz samples off the log, so a step held for under ~100 ms would not appear at all. Zoom to a few seconds around a session start to read them.

targets.rawQueryText:
SELECT time, "Substate (0x610 b7)" FROM (
  SELECT r.ts/1000.0 AS time, CASE CAST(r.value AS INTEGER) WHEN 2 THEN 'AC (0x02)' WHEN 35 THEN 'DC (0x23)' ELSE printf('0x%02X', CAST(r.value AS INTEGER)) END AS "Substate (0x610 b7)"
  FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
  WHERE s.key = 'charge_manager_state' AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to AND r.ts < 2000000000000
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM (SELECT $__from/1000.0, CASE CAST(r.value AS INTEGER) WHEN 2 THEN 'AC (0x02)' WHEN 35 THEN 'DC (0x23)' ELSE printf('0x%02X', CAST(r.value AS INTEGER)) END
                 FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
                 WHERE s.key = 'charge_manager_state' AND r.ts < $__from AND r.ts < 2000000000000
                 ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1)
)
ORDER BY time

panels.title: Charge-manager substate (0x610 b7)

panels.description: `charge_manager_error_src` (0x610 b1) and `charge_manager_error_code` (0x610 b2-3, signed 16 LE). Three episodes exist in the whole 29-session corpus: (7, 1101) on 2026-08-02, (8, 1101) on 2026-08-08, and (7, 853) on 2026-08-09 14:41:46 — the aborted DC attempt, which ran 43.7 s and ended 47.4 s before the first amp of the session that followed. ⚠️ `vcu_err_charge_manager` (0x100 b7 bit 1), the VCU's rollup bit, stayed 0 through all three, so it is not a substitute for watching this. Byte order matters: 853 is 0x0355 little-endian; read big-endian it would be 21 763.

targets.rawQueryText:
-- Every row of either fault field in the range, not only the non-zero ones, so the
-- moment an episode CLEARS is visible too. Both are logged raw: two sources and two
-- codes across 29 sessions is not a table anyone can name yet.
SELECT r.ts/1000.0 AS time,
       CASE s.key WHEN 'charge_manager_error_src' THEN 'CM_ERROR_SRC (b1)'
                  ELSE 'CM_ERROR_CODE (b2-3)' END AS "Field",
       r.value AS "Value",
       CASE WHEN r.value <> 0 THEN 'fault' ELSE 'clear' END AS "State"
FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
WHERE s.key IN ('charge_manager_error_src', 'charge_manager_error_code')
  AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to AND r.ts < 2000000000000
ORDER BY r.ts

AC side of the same frames

panels.description: `ac_supply_limit_a` (0x620 b1, `CM_AC_MAX_CURR`) is the supply-side ceiling — 8, 10 and 13 A here, all standard cable/pilot ratings — and it BOUNDS the setpoint rather than reporting it: `charge_limit_a` (0x10A b7 ÷ 7) never once exceeds it across the 784 508 frames where it is non-zero, and the ceiling LEADS, stepping 10 → 13 on 2026-08-08 19:40:13.9 with the setpoint following 120 ms later. 🟡 It is not the mains current: it matches floor(`mains_a`) in only 12 % of frames and sat at 13 through a 6.8 h session drawing 1.4 A. Included here because the same five frames carry the AC session too — `fast_dc_target_a` is 0 in 100.000 % of the 783 310 AC frames, so the DC panels above go flat and this is where an AC charge shows up.

targets.rawQueryText:
-- The AC ceiling, the setpoint it bounds, and the current actually drawn.
SELECT time, metric, value FROM (
  SELECT r.ts/1000.0 AS time,
         CASE s.key
                WHEN 'ac_supply_limit_a' THEN 'supply ceiling (0x620 b1)'
                WHEN 'charge_limit_a' THEN 'setpoint (0x10A b7)'
                WHEN 'mains_a' THEN 'mains current (0x305)'
         END AS metric,
         r.value AS value
  FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
  WHERE s.key IN ('ac_supply_limit_a', 'charge_limit_a', 'mains_a') AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to AND r.ts < 2000000000000
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM (SELECT r.ts/1000.0, 'supply ceiling (0x620 b1)', r.value
                 FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
                 WHERE s.key = 'ac_supply_limit_a' AND r.ts < $__from AND r.ts < 2000000000000
                 ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM (SELECT r.ts/1000.0, 'setpoint (0x10A b7)', r.value
                 FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
                 WHERE s.key = 'charge_limit_a' AND r.ts < $__from AND r.ts < 2000000000000
                 ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM (SELECT r.ts/1000.0, 'mains current (0x305)', r.value
                 FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
                 WHERE s.key = 'mains_a' AND r.ts < $__from AND r.ts < 2000000000000
                 ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM (SELECT $__to/1000.0, 'supply ceiling (0x620 b1)', r.value
                 FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
                 WHERE s.key = 'ac_supply_limit_a' AND r.ts <= $__to AND r.ts < 2000000000000
                 ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM (SELECT $__to/1000.0, 'setpoint (0x10A b7)', r.value
                 FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
                 WHERE s.key = 'charge_limit_a' AND r.ts <= $__to AND r.ts < 2000000000000
                 ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM (SELECT $__to/1000.0, 'mains current (0x305)', r.value
                 FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
                 WHERE s.key = 'mains_a' AND r.ts <= $__to AND r.ts < 2000000000000
                 ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1)
)
ORDER BY time
